about.title: Palo Alto Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Palo Alto is a city built around innovation, but that same density of consumer goods, tech hardware, vehicles, and household products means defective items can and do cause serious harm here. Whether it's a malfunctioning e-bike battery near Alma Street, a failed airbag in a collision along Middlefield Road, or a household appliance that catches fire, California law gives injured residents a real path to accountability. Unlike many personal injury claims, product liability cases often rely on strict liability, meaning the injured person typically doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, just that the product was defective and caused harm. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect Palo Alto residents with independent attorneys who evaluate these claims for free. If a product hurt you or someone in your family, preserving the item and getting informed quickly can matter. We help make that first connection simple, with no upfront cost and no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Palo Alto Residents Reach Out to Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: California often applies strict liability to defective products, so you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties an attorney may pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Attorneys in our network can advise you on keeping the defective item intact, since physical evidence is often central to proving design, manufacturing, or warning defects.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims frequently rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. An independent attorney can review your specific situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in its current condition and avoid repairs or alterations. The product itself is often key evidence in Palo Alto claims, whether it's a defective e-bike battery or a household item. Store it safely and let an attorney advise you on next steps.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We simply help match Palo Alto residents with independent attorneys who handle these claims.
